title: Exploiting the Margin: How Capitalism Fuels AI at the Expense of Minoritized Groups

bias_targets.methodology: Applying the theoretical framework of racial capitalism to analyze existing literature and case studies, such as the 2019 NIST facial recognition study and the Google Gemini chatbot incident.

Analyzing case studies of labor exploitation in the AI supply chain (e.g., gig workers, data labelers) and the discriminatory outcomes of automated social services like the Allegheny Family Screening Tool on low-income populations.
Reviewing existing literature (e.g., Simone Browne's work) to highlight elevated facial recognition error rates for women and the misclassification of gender intersecting with race.
Citing existing studies demonstrating elevated algorithmic error rates for the elderly and the young compared to middle-aged white men.
Examining a historical case study (Brandon Mayfield) to illustrate how AI systems and surveillance algorithms can perpetuate harmful stereotypes based on religious beliefs and conversions.
